section_2_effects_by_kind.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION

Z2_forced.incidence_forest: adds edge (current_orbit, target_hex); merges iff target_hex already registered elsewhere
Z2_forced.hub_touch_count: +1 iff target_hex == hub_id exactly; +0 for any other hub-component hexagon
Z2_forced.F_H: both unchanged when forced (non-abandoning by construction)
Z2_forced.future_R2_source_orbit: UNCHANGED -- walk remains in same orbit, R2 fired immediately after would still source from this orbit at a later phase

Z3_forced.incidence_forest: adds edge (fresh_orbit, target_hex); merges the fresh orbit (not the source) iff target_hex already registered elsewhere
Z3_forced.future_R2_source_orbit: CHANGED -- walk is now positioned in the fresh orbit; R2 fired immediately after sources from there instead

R.R_budget: consumes the sole remaining slot; r_count 1->2, terminal
R.incidence_forest: adds edge (reentered_orbit, target_hex) to an already-registered orbit -- this is precisely what target_a_recognizer's same_component check evaluates
R.hub_touch_count: same single-hexagon rule; this edge IS the one being judged against the <=2 cap
R.F_H: evaluated by target_a_recognizer's own F_def_equals_1/H_equals_0 gates on the resulting state
R.future_R2_source_orbit: n/a -- this edge is R2 or R1 itself

section_2_effects_by_kind.sharpest_asymmetry: Z2 can grow the merged territory while leaving the future R2 source orbit unchanged; Z3 cannot -- firing Z3 necessarily relocates the walk, bundling any merge it achieves with a changed R2-source-orbit candidate

section_3_merge_requirements.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
section_3_merge_requirements.direct_touch_vs_intermediate: not required to be direct; a true two-hop bridge through a third orbit is geometrically possible (revisiting an orbit's unused phases across non-consecutive steps) but requires TWO separate joints through the same orbit vertex, not one -- strictly more expensive than the one-step version, and unnecessary if a one-step coincidence exists
section_3_merge_requirements.before_or_after_completer: irrelevant to the mechanism -- the completer only matters because it is the event that first sets hub_touch_count from 0 to 1 and fixes hub_id's identity; the merge machinery applies identically to every joint regardless of position relative to the completer
section_3_merge_requirements.alters_future_R2_source_orbit: only if the merge is achieved via Z3; a Z2-mediated merge leaves the source orbit fixed

lemma_A.text: Z2 cannot connect the isolated R1-target component to the hub without changing the future R2 source
lemma_A.counterpattern: Z2 is orbit-preserving by definition; if its forced target phase's hexagon happens to already be registered in hub's component via another orbit, this single Z2 edge merges the components while the walk's current orbit (hence any immediately-following R2's source orbit) is unchanged -- exactly the case the lemma claims cannot exist
lemma_A.unresolved_scope: whether such a coincidental hexagon actually exists within any of the 8 children's R1-target orbit's unvisited phase set is NOT verified here -- refuted at the rule level, not shown realized in any concrete instance

lemma_B.text: any Z3-fresh merge into the hub component causes an F or hub-touch violation
lemma_B.counterpattern: hub_touch_count increments only for the single hexagon hub_id (0 for all 8), never for any other hexagon in hub's larger incidence component (e.g. short_ell2_r1_70's hub component has 9 hexagons: 0,1,4,6,8,9,18,24,96); a forced Z3 targeting e.g. hexagon 96 or 18 would merge into hub's component while leaving hub_touch_count untouched, and a forced (non-abandoning) Z3 never increments F regardless of target hexagon
lemma_B.unresolved_scope: existence of the specific geometric coincidence for any of the 8 children not verified here

lemma_C.text: any legal two-step component bridge consumes geometry needed for R2
lemma_C.reasoning: read literally ('any... bridge') false: R-budget moot for Z2/Z3, F/H moot for forced joints, hub_touch_count moot provided the bridge avoids hexagon hub_id specifically. A well-chosen one-step bridge consumes none of the four resources target_a_recognizer gates on. The universal claim is refuted; the genuine, avoidable risk it points at is real only in the special case where the bridge re-touches hub_id specifically, which would consume the one remaining hub-touch slot (the completer already spent the first of two allowed)

lemma_D.text: the isolated component can only merge through an orbit already absent from the required incidence forest

reading_1.interpretation: only a fresh/never-registered orbit (i.e. only Z3) can bridge
reading_1.counterpattern: same as Lemma A -- Z2 reuses the already-registered R1-target orbit and is an equally valid bridge mechanism

reading_2.interpretation: the bridging orbit must be a 'sacrificial' one distinct from R2's own eventual target orbit
reading_2.reasoning: nothing in evaluate_edge or target_a_recognizer distinguishes a sacrificial bridging orbit from R2's eventual target orbit; whether a specific path reuses the same orbit for both purposes is a fact about which continuations are legal from a given state, requiring a continuation trace to settle, not attempted here
